q: 1. The water obtained from ............. is generally known as sub-surface water.
explain: Artesian wells tap into confined aquifers where water is under pressure, making it a primary source of sub-surface water.

q: 2. The quantity of water available from an infiltration gallery depends upon the .............
explain: Yield depends on the length/size of the gallery, the permeability of the soil, and the recharging capacity of the source.

q: 3. The layers such as lime stone and sandstone which do not allow the water to pass through them are known as .............
explain: An aquiclude is a geological formation which is porous but relatively impermeable, preventing the easy flow of water.

q: 4. The open wells or dug wells are also known as .............
explain: Dug wells are often shallow and rely on water percolating through the surrounding soil into the well shaft.

q: 5. The yield of a surface stream may be obtained by .............
explain: All these methods are standard engineering practices to measure the discharge or flow rate of surface water bodies.

q: 6. Freeman formula for estimating, the fire demand (Q) in liters per minutes is given by .............
explain: Freeman's formula calculates fire flow where P is the population in thousands.

q: 7. According to Kuichling formula, the fire demand (Q) in liters per minute is given by .............
explain: Kuichling's formula for fire demand is expressed as Q = 3182√P.

q: 8. pH value is a symbol for ............. concentration.
explain: pH is defined as the negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration ($-log[H^+]$).

q: 9. The most common cause of acidity in water is .............
explain: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid ($H_2CO_3$), which is the most frequent source of acidity in natural waters.

q: 10. The maximum permissible fluorine content in water for domestic supplies should be .............
explain: While small amounts of fluoride prevent dental caries, levels above 1.5 ppm can cause dental fluorosis (mottling of teeth).

q: 11. In the process of screening, the screens should be inclined at an angle of .............
explain: Inclining the screens increases the effective area and makes manual cleaning with a rake much easier.

q: 12. Plain sedimentation is a process of retaining water in a basin so that the suspended particles settles down as a result of the .............
options: action of velocity of the particles
explain: Sedimentation relies on gravity to pull particles heavier than water to the bottom of the tank.

q: 13. The most common coagulant is .............
explain: Alum (Aluminium Sulphate) is preferred because it is effective, relatively cheap, and easy to handle.

q: 14. The coefficient of uniformity for slow sand filters is .............
explain: Uniformity coefficient ($C_u = D_{60}/D_{10}$) should be around 1.75 to 2.5 for slow sand filters to ensure even voids.

q: 15. Cleaning of rapid sand filters is done by .............
options: scraping the top layer of filter media
explain: Unlike slow sand filters which are scraped, rapid sand filters are cleaned by forceful backwashing with water and sometimes air.

q: 16. The most commonly used disinfectant for drinking water throughout the world is .............
explain: Chlorine is used globally because it is effective, provides a residual effect in pipes, and is relatively inexpensive.

q: 17. The ideal method of disinfection of swimming pool water is by .............
explain: Ozone is a very powerful oxidant that leaves no unpleasant 'chlorine smell' or taste, making it ideal for high-end swimming pools.

q: 18. Pre-chlorination .............
explain: Adding chlorine at the start of the treatment process helps oxidize organic matter, improving the performance of subsequent stages.

q: 19. The permanent hardness in water is caused due to the salts like .............
explain: Non-carbonate (permanent) hardness is caused by chlorides, nitrates, and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.

q: 20. By lime soda process, hardness can be reduced to less than .............
explain: While Zeolite reaches zero hardness, the chemical Lime-Soda process typically reduces it to about 30-50 ppm.

q: 21. In order to control the flow of water through pipes, a ............... is provided.
explain: Gate valves (also known as sluice valves) are used to start or stop the flow of water; they are used as isolation valves rather than for throttling.

q: 22. A source of colour in water is due to
explain: Decomposing organic debris (leaves, wood) releases tannins and humic substances that colour the water.

q: 23. Purest water may have
explain: Because water molecules absorb red light more than blue, very pure, deep water often appears to have a faint blue or green tint.

q: 24. Highly coloured waters are
explain: While color might not always mean danger, it is 'unaesthetic'—consumers will likely reject it based on its appearance.

q: 25. Coloured waters may affect the following water treatment unit
explain: Colouring matter can react with chlorine, exerting a chlorine demand and potentially forming disinfection by-products.

q: 26. Permissible colour for drinking water is not more than
explain: Standard drinking water guidelines typically set the limit for colour at 10 to 15 True Colour Units (TCU).

q: 27. Turbidity is mainly due to
explain: Suspended solids (silt, clay, etc.) are the primary contributors to measurable turbidity.

q: 28. Turbidity is undesirable because it
explain: High turbidity blocks sunlight, which inhibits the growth of aquatic plants and algae by preventing photosynthesis.

q: 29. Turbidity can be removed by
explain: The combination of chemical coagulation (clumping small particles together) and filtration is the standard method for removing turbidity.

q: 30. The usual size of suspended solids is
explain: Suspended solids generally range from 1 μm to 100 μm; particles smaller than 1 μm are typically classified as colloids.

q: 31. pH of water sample containing 0.0001 (10^-1) g of H ion per litre is
explain: pH is defined as $-log_{10}[H^+]$. If $[H^+] = 10^{-1}$, then $pH = 1$.

q: 32. Caustic alkalinity is because of
explain: Caustic alkalinity refers specifically to the alkalinity contributed by hydroxide ($OH^-$) ions.

q: 33. Phenolphthalein end point represents
explain: Titrating to the phenolphthalein end point (pH 8.3) measures all the hydroxide and exactly half of the carbonate alkalinity.

q: 34. Excess alkalinity is undesirable in swimming pools because
options: lacrimal fluid around the eye is altered
explain: High alkalinity can alter the pH of the fluid around the eyes, leading to stinging and irritation for swimmers.

q: 35. pH range of mineral acidity is
explain: Mineral acidity (caused by strong acids like $H_2SO_4$ or $HCl$) is present when the pH is below 4.5.

q: 36. A buffer is that
explain: A buffer solution is a system that resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.

q: 37. Eutrophication of a lake is ...........
options: enrichment of water quality with nutrients
deterioration of water bodies with biological growths
explain: Eutrophication is the process where a water body becomes overly enriched with nutrients (like phosphorus and nitrogen), leading to excessive growth of plants and algae.

q: 38. 'Dental caries' will be absent where the following is present ...........
explain: Mottled enamel (Fluorosis) occurs when there is an excess of fluoride. While aesthetically displeasing, teeth with fluorosis are highly resistant to dental caries (cavities).

q: 39. Concentration of fluorides desirable in water is ...........
explain: A small amount of fluoride (roughly 1 to 1.5 mg/l) is desirable to prevent tooth decay. Values exceeding 1.5-2.0 mg/l lead to mottling of teeth.

q: 40. In drinking water number of coliform bacteria should not exceed ...........
explain: For treated drinking water, the standard limit is strict: there should be zero coliforms per 100 ml of sample to ensure safety from pathogens.

q: 41. For an old city with constraints for growth the best method of forecasting future population is ...........
explain: The Arithmetical Increase Method assumes a constant rate of growth and is most suitable for old, large cities that have reached their saturation point and have limited room for expansion.

q: 42. If the present population of a city is 'a', rate of increase per decade is 'b', incremental increase per decade is 'c', percentage growth per decade is 'r', then population after 'n' decades by incremental increase method is ...........
explain: The incremental increase method combines the arithmetic increase ('b' per decade) with the average of the net increments ('c'). The formula is Pn = P + n.X + [n(n+1)/2].Y.

q: 43. River water may have ...........
options: more suspended solids and less dissolved solids
more dissolved solids and less suspended solids
more dissolved solids and less floating solids
explain: Surface waters like rivers are exposed to runoff, which brings in high amounts of suspended silt and clay, but they generally have lower contact time with minerals compared to groundwater.

q: 44. Permissible velocity through coarse screens is not greater than ...........
explain: The velocity through the openings of a coarse screen (rack) is typically kept around 0.75 to 1 m/s. Higher velocities might force debris through the bars, while lower velocities cause excessive head loss.

q: 45. Generally 'flow through period' of a sedimentation tank is ...........
options: exactly equal to the detention period
sometime more and some time less
explain: The theoretical detention period (V/Q) assumes ideal flow. In reality, short-circuiting and dead zones cause the actual 'flow through period' to be less than the theoretical detention time.

q: 46. Coagulating power of a chemical increases with its ...........
explain: According to the Schulze-Hardy rule, the coagulating power of an electrolyte increases rapidly with the valency of the ion. For example, $Al^{3+}$ is much more effective than $Na^+$.

q: 47. Mud balls are formed in a filter because of ...........
options: raw water rolling over the filter surface
bond developed between impurities and sand grains due to inefficient back washing
explain: If backwashing is insufficient, sticky organic matter and silt accumulate on sand grains, forming clumps or 'mud balls' that sink and clog the filter bed.

q: 48. 'Pre-chlorination' is done to ...........
explain: Pre-chlorination (adding chlorine before filtration) helps control algae growth in basins, oxidizes iron/manganese, and reduces tastes and odors caused by organic matter.

q: 49. A disadvantage of ozone is ............
options: impurities are oxidized before disinfection commences
toxic end products are given out
explain: Ozone is highly unstable and has a very short half-life, meaning it must be generated on-site and cannot provide a residual disinfecting effect in the distribution system.

q: 50. Hardness is removed from water based on the relative insolubility of the following ............
explain: In the lime-soda process, calcium is precipitated as Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) and magnesium is precipitated as Magnesium Hydroxide (Mg(OH)2) due to their low solubility at high pH.

q: 51. Mg(OH)2 gets precipitated at a pH of ............
explain: Magnesium removal requires a much higher alkalinity; it typically begins to precipitate effectively only when the pH reaches approximately 11.

q: 52. To active the zeolite bed the following is done ............
explain: When the zeolite resin is exhausted, it is 'regenerated' by passing a brine (sodium chloride) solution through it to restore its sodium ions.

q: 53. Blow off values are a must when ............
explain: Blow-off valves (scour valves) are placed at dead ends to flush out accumulated sediment and stagnant water.

q: 54. 'Biological magnification' is ............
options: decrease in concentration with trophic level
increase in concentration with trophic level
explain: Biomagnification is the process where certain toxins (like mercury or DDT) become more concentrated as they move up the food chain.
